transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that... on these late work nights, I’ll order what I tell myself is just dinner. But it ends up turning into a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then extra snacks from my kitchen on top of that. It's just way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting across from me.
After one of these large eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to 'undo' it—like make yourself vomit, use laxatives, fast the next day, or exercise excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that. I just... I usually feel really full and uncomfortable, and I might skip breakfast the next morning just because I'm not hungry, but I don't try to make myself throw up or exercise a bunch or anything. I just kind of deal with feeling bad about it.
How often do these large eating episodes happen, and how long has this pattern been going on?

Well, when I actually look back at my delivery receipts and my work calendar, there’s usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes it's more than that. And... I'd say that specific pattern has been going on for several months now.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're consuming, even if you want to?

Yeah, I definitely do. Once I start... there’s this point where I’m just kind of watching myself keep going back to the food, or opening another package. In my head, I'm thinking that I really should stop, but it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't seem to stop myself once I'm in that mode.
